sections.h2: Where is Rome, and why is the city so large?
sections.html:
Rome sits in Oneida County in central New York and shares the Utica-Rome metro area with Utica. Its 75.7 square miles rank second among New York cities by area. With that much area, the Census Bureau's 2020 density is only 429.2 people per square mile.

Rome's 2020 population of 32,127 has slipped 1.4 percent, to an estimated 31,682. The state legislature turned the Town of Rome into a city on February 23, 1870. The city's ZIP codes include 13440, 13441 and 13442, plus 13308 for Blossvale and 13478 for Verona, so confirm the municipality on your deed and tax bill before you list.

sections.h2: What is Rome's history, and how does it show up in housing?
sections.html:
Rome grew up at the Oneida Carrying Place, an ancient portage between the Mohawk River and Wood Creek. The British built Fort Stanwix there in 1758, and the Continental forces held it through a 21-day siege in August 1777. The National Park Service rebuilt the fort between 1973 and 1976 and runs it as a museum.

Construction of the Erie Canal began in Rome on July 4, 1817, and the first cheese factory in the country opened here in 1851. Metal shops later earned the city the nickname "Copper City," with Rome turning out about 10 percent of the copper used in the United States. Griffiss Air Force Base ran from 1942 to 1995. Rome Free Academy, the public high school, moved onto former base land in 2002.

Houses of very different ages sit inside one city boundary, so a buyer's first question is usually when the house was built and what has been replaced since.

sections.h2: How pricey is a Rome house, and how many owners live in them?
sections.html:
The 2020-2024 Census Bureau survey values a typical Rome home at $154,400, and 56.6 percent of households are owners. Rent runs $909, and household income at the midpoint is $59,925.

  • 13,870 households with 2.13 people apiece
  • Residents 65 and older account for 19.8 percent
  • Poverty affects 18.1 percent of residents
  • Owner costs come to $1,431 a month with a loan and $701 with none

At that price level a major repair is a large share of a house's value, so owners sometimes weigh an as-is sale against fixing up first.

Griffiss closed as a base in 1995 under the federal realignment process, but the site still houses the Rome Laboratory, now part of the Air Force Research Laboratory, and the Eastern Air Defense Sector. The old airstrip is Griffiss Airport, which has general aviation and military use but no scheduled commercial service.

Other local anchors include Rome Memorial Hospital, a 129-bed hospital, and AmeriCU Credit Union, which is headquartered in the city. In 2022 Rome's health and social-service providers took in $1.01 billion and its retailers $665 million. Workers average only 18.0 minutes to reach their jobs.

sections.h2: How do roads, trains and weather shape a sale in Rome?
sections.html:
The Utica-Rome Expressway, a 14-mile stretch of Route 49, runs from Rome to Utica, where it meets I-90 and several state routes. Routes 26, 46, 49 and 69 meet downtown. Amtrak's Empire Service stops in Rome twice a day in each direction, and CENTRO runs six bus routes in the city.

Winters are the main stress on a house here. Rome's climate table shows about 102 inches of snow in an average year and 56.7 snowy days, with January lows averaging 12.9 degrees. A tornado rated EF2 hit the center of the city on July 16, 2024, damaged roofs and brick buildings, and prompted emergency declarations from the city, county and state. If your house was damaged then, keep repair invoices and insurance paperwork together for a buyer.

sections.h2: Which permits does Rome require for work on a house?
sections.html:
Rome's Code Enforcement office issues building permits and inspects work under the state's Uniform Fire Prevention and Building Code. It says to contact the office whenever you are not sure a project needs a permit.

  • Permits are generally required for new windows, kitchen and bath remodels, decks, porches and steps, pools, chimney work and any plumbing or electrical change.
  • A stop work order is issued to any job started without a permit, and fees double for work that began first.
  • Accessory structures under 144 square feet need a permit but carry no fee.
  • All plumbing must be done by a City of Rome licensed plumber.

Pools holding 24 inches of water or more need a permit, and a pool without its electrical inspection cannot get a Certificate of Compliance. Housing inspectors assigned to each ward handle property maintenance and zoning enforcement, and multiple dwellings of three units or more get fire safety and property maintenance inspections at least every three years.

sections.h2: When are Rome property taxes due?
sections.html:
Rome's city treasurer collects city, school and county taxes on a set calendar, and city taxes may include water, sewer and refuse charges. The city's printed schedule gives these dates.

City of Rome property tax due dates (City Treasurer schedule)
DateWhat is due
January 31Metered water and sewer, special assessments
February 28County tax
April 30City tax first half, school tax second half
July 31Metered water and sewer
October 31City tax second half, school tax first half

The October 31 date for 2026 has passed, so the next dates are January 31 and February 28, 2027. The Treasurer's Office, in City Hall at 198 North Washington Street, can send a duplicate bill at 315-339-7689. On the assessment side, the Assessor's page lists 13,325 properties, a 2026 taxable total of $898,330,496, and grievance day on the first Tuesday in August.

sections.h2: What extra step does Rome add before a deed is recorded?
sections.html:
Rome has one extra step before the county will take a deed. The Oneida County Clerk requires the deed itself to be stamped by the Rome City Assessor first, at 198 North Washington Street, Suite 1B (315-339-7614).

The clerk's land recording page then lists a $45 statutory fee, $5 for each page, a $5 TP-584 filing fee and a $125 real property transfer report fee for residential property. A deed needs a legal description, the full names and physical addresses of both parties, and original notarized signatures. White-out or redaction means rejection. If you must correct an error, the clerk suggests drawing a new deed.

sections.h2: What is the fastest way to sell a Rome house?
sections.html:
Hiring an agent, selling on your own and taking a cash bid are the choices. With the midpoint home near $154,000, repair bills, a vacant house through a Rome winter and a sales commission each take a big bite of what you keep.

  • Choose an agent when the house shows well and you are happy to wait on a buyer's loan.
  • Choose a sale by owner if you will manage the Property Condition Disclosure Statement and the contract yourself.
  • Price out a cash bid for a home with postponed repairs, storm damage, tenants or a probate matter.

Hand the state disclosure statement to the buyer before a contract is signed. Late or missing delivery means a $500 price credit for the buyer.

faqs.q: Does a Rome deed need a stamp from the city assessor?
faqs.a: Yes. The Oneida County Clerk requires deeds for Rome properties to be stamped by the Rome City Assessor before recording. Allow time for that step before closing.

faqs.q: Does the 2024 tornado affect how I sell a Rome house?
faqs.a: It can. A high-end EF2 tornado crossed the city on July 16, 2024, and damaged roofs and brick buildings. Keep repair invoices and permits to show a buyer.

faqs.q: Which school district serves a Rome address?
faqs.a: The Rome City School District covers most of the city and runs Rome Free Academy. Oriskany, Sherrill and Westmoreland districts cover other parts, so look at the tax bill.

faqs.q: Whom do I contact if a Rome tax bill never arrives?
faqs.a: Call the City Treasurer's Office at 315-339-7689 for a duplicate. Checks go to the City of Rome at 198 North Washington Street.

faqs.q: Is a permit required for window replacement in Rome?
faqs.a: Yes, generally. The Code Enforcement page lists new windows among the work that requires a permit because of energy code and egress rules, and doubled fees apply if work starts first.
